messages:
Maya: quick heads-up — my docs PR can't merge, docs-preview linkcheck is failing on an SDK example. CI shows a broken/escaped URL inside a fenced code block and the linter treats it as a dead link :grimacing:

jordan: can you paste the snippet? might be a markdown parsing quirk or linkchecker config.

Maya: yup — reproduced in preview. snippet is this:```js
// example: calling responses API
const res = await client.responses.create({
  model: 'open-llm/v1',
  input: 'Summarize',
});
console.log(res.reasonUrl); // <-- added for demo, points to https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/blob/main/README.md#usage
```

Sam: ah — linkcheck treats code-block URLs differently? It shouldn't fail on raw URLs in fenced blocks but our linkchecker flags repo anchors if they don't exist. Is that header added in the target README?

Maya: the anchor exists locally but the generated preview mangles the anchor id (spaces -> hyphens vs underscores). So linkcheck says 404. CI blocks merge by policy.

Priya: short term: wrap the URL in angle brackets <...> or replace with a placeholder in the snippet (e.g., <EXAMPLE_DOC_LINK>) and add a real link in the prose. That avoids failing linkcheck while keeping the example valid. Longer term we should tweak linkcheck to ignore code fences.

Maya: thanks. small question — while I update the snippet, one blocker remains: the text references `res.reason` as a field returned by runtime when generation is truncated. I asked runtime team earlier but no reply yet — docs reviewers are waiting for that confirmation before approving the wording about the shape of the response object. @Jordan any idea?

Jordan: IIRC runtime includes `status` and a short `reason` string on aborted responses, but shape changed across versions. Which target config is this doc for (hosted API v1 vs dedicated v1)?

Maya: hosted API examples — targetting the stable v1 surface. The PR copy says: "When the model aborts, responses include `status: 'aborted'` and `reason: <string>`." Reviewers want a precise example.

Jordan: ok. I can ping runtime-engineering. @Sam can you confirm current hosted API shape? If it's still `status` + `reason` that's fine. If not, we should show a small defensive snippet:```js
if (res.status === 'aborted') {
  // reason may be present, check safely
  console.warn(res.reason || res.error || 'aborted without reason');
}
```

Sam: checking — posted in eng-runtime thread, but quick answer: hosted v1 returns `status` and an optional `reason` string for common abort causes (e.g., token_limit, content_filter). We also added `error` for internal failures in the last minor bump. So docs should reflect optional `reason` and fallback to `error` where appropriate.

Maya: perfect, I'll update the snippet to avoid the direct link (use placeholder + prose link) and change example to the defensive pattern with comment mentioning optional fields. That should satisfy reviewers.

docs-bot: Docs preview updated for PR #4217 — linkcheck: 1 failed -> now ignored for code-block URLs (temporary) — run id 2026-03-21-ops

Maya: great — thanks everyone :tada: I'll push the patch and re-request review.

Jordan: ping me when it's pushed, I'll approve if CI is green.

Sam: nice. if runtime team confirms stable behavior in the next 24h we can merge once linkcheck passes.

Priya: follow-up: file a small issue to relax linkcheck for fenced code URLs (docs backlog) so this doesn't keep blocking future snippets.
